key_insight: Initial vorticity packing fraction (VPF) remains the main driver of Eulerian–Lagrangian coupling in the inverse-cascade regime, but at late times and across broader Reynolds numbers the tracer-transport order becomes strongly Re-dependent and the simple correspondence breaks down.
engineering_relevance: For 2D decaying Navier–Stokes systems, both initial vortex packing and Reynolds number must be accounted for when predicting mixing, transport, and coherence in reduced-order models or flow-control studies.
method: Parameter sweep over initial vorticity packing fraction (VPF) and Reynolds number (Re) in decaying 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes flows.
Compare Eulerian flow statistics with Lagrangian tracer-particle transport across nonequilibrium inverse-cascade and late-time coherent-vortex regimes.
Assess whether transport ordering by VPF persists or weakens as Re varies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic transport increase with VPF in the inverse-cascade regime, but strong oscillatory and nonmonotonic Re dependence in the late-time regime, based on the explored (VPF, Re) parameter space, resolutions, and integration times.
watch_item: The conclusion is limited to the parameter range, spatial resolutions, and simulation times studied, so the observed breakdown of direct Eulerian–Lagrangian correspondence may not generalize outside that domain.
paper_title: Eulerian Lagrangian relations in decaying two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes fluids across initial vorticity packing and Reynolds number
